main_body: Two stacked/adjacent wooden crates, each with a plank-striped lid on top and a dark front face with a diagonal brace
top_band: Light tan plank-striped lid (L 146/113 alternating, #b98a55/#99683a), rows 1-8 at x=7 and x=15; rows 9-14 at x=22 for the second crate
evidence: The column at x=15 shows a light lid (rows 1-8), then a distinct dark edge row 9 (L=44), then a much darker front face (rows 10-16, L=65) with a lighter diagonal brace and a bottom shadow. The step from top to front is about 80 L, so the lid reads as a separate horizontal surface. The lid is tall for a foreshortened top (8 of 19 rows), but the crate is roughly cubic and the dark edge row under it acts as an eave shadow. The front face is painted flat with no inset, but the top and front are both clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The wood has about 3 tones on the lid and 2-3 on the front, with no grain, nail or knot dots. The front face is a near-uniform dark brown with a single diagonal brace line. Outlines are tinted dark brown (only 12% neutral), which is acceptable, but the piece is clearly thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references.
